EXERCICE1

```{r}

# Charger les librairies
library(FactoMineR)

library(GGally)

library(readxl)
# Charger la base de données

wine <- read_excel("wine.xlsx")

View(wine)

# examiner les dimensions (nombre de lignes et nombre de colonnes) de la base
dim(wine)

# Visualiser les 5 prémières lignes de la base de données
head(wine, 5)


# Supprimer la colonne de la variable target
wine <- wine[, -14]

# head(wine, 5) # pour verifier l'opération

# Examiner la matrice de diagramme de dispersion

ggpairs(wine)

# Réaliser l'ACP

ResACP <- PCA(wine, graph = FALSE)
ResACP

# Extraire les Valeurs propres de l'ACP
ResACP$eig

# Extraire le tableau des corrélations des variables avec les Composantes Principales
ResACP$var$cor

# Afficher le cercle des corrélation des variables avec les Composante Principales 1 & 2

plot(ResACP, choix = "var", axes = c(1, 2))


# Afficher  les axes des Composante Principales 1 & 2
plot(ResACP, choix = "ind", axes = c(1, 2))


```

EXERCICE2

```{r}
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))

#Charger les librairies

library(readxl)
library(FactoMineR)


#Charger les données

housetasks <- read_excel("housetasks.xlsx")
Data <-housetasks

View(housetasks)

names(Data)

head(Data,1)



# Table de Contingence

#DataAFC <- Data[-1, ]
DataAFC <- Data[ ,-1]



View(DataAFC)

dim(DataAFC) #dimension 


#  Exécuter l'analyse factorielle des correspondances (AFC)
CAResults1 <- CA(DataAFC,graph = FALSE)

#Afficher les résultats de l'analyse des correspondances.
summary(CAResults1)


# Modifier les noms des colonnes
rownames(CAResults1$row$coord) <- c("Cooking", "Laundry","Cleaning","Shopping", "Ironing","Finances","Reepairs","Driving","Gardening","Homework","Dishes")


# Visualiser le résultat sur le biplot
plot.CA(CAResults1, axes = c(1, 2))

```

EXERCICE3:ACM

```{r}
#Charger les librairies
library(readxl)

library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library("corrplot")

# Charger les données
adult_clean <- read_excel("adult_clean.xlsx")
View(adult_clean)

data <-adult_clean
attach(data)
View(data)


#'In the R code below, the MCA is performed only on the active
#'individuals/variables :
res.mca <- MCA(data, graph = FALSE)
print(res.mca)


#Valeurs propres
eig.val <- get_eigenvalue(res.mca)
head(eig.val)
eig.val

#Inertie des variables
fviz_screeplot(res.mca, addlabels = TRUE, ylim = c(0, 45))

#'Graphe des individus et des variables categorielles
fviz_mca_biplot(res.mca,repel = TRUE, ggtheme = theme_minimal())

#'Graphe des variables

var <- get_mca_var(res.mca)
var
summary(res.mca)
#'The different components can be accessed as follow:
# Coordinates
var$coord
# Cos2: quality on the factore map
var$cos2
# Contributions to the principal components
var$contrib


#'Correlation between variables and principal dimensions
#'To visualize the correlation between variables 
#'and MCA principal dimensions, type this:
fviz_mca_var(res.mca, choice = "mca.cor", 
             repel = TRUE, # Avoid text overlapping (slow)
             ggtheme = theme_minimal())

#'Coordinates of variable categories
#'The R code below displays the coordinates of each variable 
#'categories in each dimension (1, 2 and 3):
head(round(var$coord, 2), 4)

#'Use the function fviz_mca_var() [in factoextra] 
#'to visualize only variable categories:
#fviz_mca_var(res.mca, 
#           repel = TRUE, # Avoid text overlapping (slow)
#             ggtheme = theme_minimal())


#'It’s possible to change the color and the shape of the variable points using the arguments col.var and shape.var as follow:
#fviz_mca_var(res.mca, col.var="black", shape.var = 15,
 #            repel = TRUE)


#'Quality of representation of variable categories
#
head(var$cos2)


fviz_mca_var(res.mca, col.var = "cos2",
             gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"), 
             repel = TRUE, # Avoid text overlapping
             ggtheme = theme_minimal())



# Change the transparency by cos2 values
#fviz_mca_var(res.mca, alpha.var="cos2",
  #           repel = TRUE,
 #            ggtheme = theme_minimal())

#'You can visualize the cos2 of row categories on all the dimensions 
#'using the corrplot package:

corrplot(var$cos2, is.corr=FALSE)

#'It’s also possible to create a bar plot of variable cos2 
#'using the function fviz_cos2()[in factoextra]:

# Cos2 of variable categories on Dim.1 and Dim.2
#fviz_cos2(res.mca, choice = "var", axes = 1:2)
```

EXERCICE4 :AFDM

```{r}
#' Clear the workspace
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))

#' Packages
library(readxl)

library(FactoMineR)
library(ggplot2)
library(factoextra)
library(PCAmixdata)
library(base)

# Import data

bank <- read_excel("bank.xlsx")
View(bank)

dim(bank)

head(bank,10)
str(bank)

#Basic Statistics of dataset 
summary(bank)

#' Perform the analyse and
#' obtain the results on the each type of variables  and on the individuals 
res.famd <- FAMD(bank, graph = FALSE)
summary (res.famd)

#****Visualiation****# 
# the respective projection of variables and individuals on  the selected principal components
fviz_famd_var(res.famd)  # Graph of variables

#fviz_famd_ind(res.famd,c(1,2))  # Graph of individuals

# Graphical Representation for the eigenvalue 
fviz_eig(res.famd) 
# Graphical representation of the contribution of variables on each axis
fviz_contrib(res.famd, choice ="var",axes = 1) 
fviz_contrib(res.famd, choice ="var",axes = 2)
# Graphical representation of the contribution of individuals  on each axis
fviz_contrib(res.famd, choice ="ind",axes = 1) 
fviz_contrib(res.famd, choice ="ind",axes = 2) 



```
